findings.explanation: Splunkbase 5167 is 'Upgrade Universal Forwarder (Windows)'; Splunk Connect for Kubernetes is a GitHub Helm chart that reached End of Support on 1 January 2024.
findings.suggested_fix: Name the Splunk OpenTelemetry Collector for Kubernetes (Splunkbase 6264) for istiod metrics, logs and events; remove SCK/5167.

findings.explanation: The istiod metric reference lists pilot_conflict_inbound_listener and pilot_conflict_outbound_listener_tcp_over_current_tcp (and similar suffixed variants), not a bare pilot_conflict_outbound_listener. The same section of detailedImplementation also lists pilot_xds_push_errors, which is absent; push failures are exposed through the type label of pilot_xds_pushes and pilot_total_xds_internal_errors / pilot_total_xds_rejects.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with documented series: pilot_conflict_outbound_listener_tcp_over_current_tcp (and siblings), pilot_total_xds_rejects, pilot_total_xds_internal_errors, pilot_xds_pushes by type.

findings.explanation: Listener conflicts come from Services that declare the same port with incompatible protocols; a DestinationRule with portLevelSettings changes cluster policy, not listeners, so this test will not increment any conflict gauge.
findings.quote: apply an invalid **DestinationRule** that creates a listener conflict: `kubectl apply -f - <<< '{apiVersion: networking.istio.io/v1beta1, kind: DestinationRule, ... portLevelSettings: [{port: {number: 80}}]}}}'`
findings.suggested_fix: Create two Services (or a Service and ServiceEntry) exposing the same port with conflicting protocols (e.g. tcp vs http) and check the pilot_conflict_* gauges.

findings.explanation: Audit events on the webhook-configuration objects record changes to those objects, not webhook call failures; failed admission calls surface on the audited request (e.g. a pod create rejected with 'failed calling webhook'). The prerequisite that the collector needs 'get on audit events' is also wrong: audit logs are control-plane files or cloud-provider logs, not an RBAC-readable resource.
findings.quote: collect audit events for `ValidatingWebhookConfiguration` and `MutatingWebhookConfiguration` resources. These show when the API server **fails to reach** the istiod webhook
findings.suggested_fix: Describe searching audit events for pod/config create requests with responseStatus messages containing 'failed calling webhook "*.istio.io"', collected from the API server audit log file or the managed-cluster audit log export.

findings.explanation: istiod push/validation counters and log categories are not host performance metrics and do not map to any CIM dataset the SPL uses; Application_State is also a legacy model with little current support.
findings.suggested_fix: Leave cimModels empty or document why a specific dataset applies; verify Application_State status in the current CIM manual before keeping it.

findings.explanation: Marked verified by an agent reviewer although two of the core metric names do not match the istiod reference, so the health score cannot have been validated end to end.
findings.suggested_fix: Downgrade status until an SME validates metric names against a live istiod.

findings.explanation: The in-cluster IstioOperator controller has been removed in recent Istio releases, so many clusters have no IstioOperator resource to inspect; also the UC says Istio 1.14+ while sibling UCs assume 1.18+.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `istioctl version` / `istioctl x precheck` for control-plane vs data-plane skew and align the minimum version with sibling UCs.

findings.explanation: With the default failurePolicy this blocks all pod creation in injected namespaces and config validation cluster-wide; the text does not warn that this is disruptive.
findings.quote: temporarily scale istiod to 0 replicas and attempt a pod deployment in a labeled namespace
findings.suggested_fix: Mark it as a non-production test only and suggest a dedicated test cluster.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: `metric_name IN (... "pilot_conflict_outbound_listener" ... "pilot_xds_push_errors")` uses names absent from the istiod metric reference, so push_errors and listener_conflicts are always 0 and the CRITICAL/DEGRADED push-error and conflict branches can never fire.

pilot_xds_pushes, galley_validation_* and sidecar_injection_requests_total are cumulative counters; summing raw values in 5-minute bins adds lifetime totals per scrape instead of in-window increments, and the gauge listener_conflicts is summed across ~10 scrapes per bin so one persistent conflict exceeds the >10 threshold. Use per-series deltas / mstats rate for counters and max/latest for gauges.

This UC reads `metric_value` while sibling UCs (3.5.3, 3.5.7, 3.5.8) read `value` from the same otel:metrics sourcetype; one of them is wrong for a given collector config. pilot_proxy_convergence_time_bucket is selected but never used.

summary: The control-plane narrative is detailed, but two of the metrics the health score depends on (pilot_xds_push_errors, pilot_conflict_outbound_listener) are not in the current istiod metric reference, the listener-conflict test would not produce a conflict, the audit-log guidance misdescribes how webhook failures appear, and the Splunkbase ID is wrong.
